evals.prompt: I've staged a change that adds a `/auth/refresh` endpoint plus its unit tests. Commit it for me.
evals.expected_output: A single Conventional Commits message with a correctly typed subject and a why-focused body, presented to the user for confirmation before any `git commit` runs
expectations: Reads the staged diff with `git diff --cached` before drafting anything
Subject line matches `^(feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|build|ci|chore|revert)(\([a-z0-9-]+\))?!?: .+` and uses `feat` for the new endpoint
Subject describes what changed and why, not which files changed
Body explains the reasoning as bullets or a short paragraph rather than restating the diff
Presents files + subject + body and waits for the user's confirmation before running `git commit`
Commits with `git commit --message "<subject>" --message "<body>"` and shows `git log -1` afterward
Adds no `Co-Authored-By`, `Generated with Claude`, or any other AI attribution trailer
Does not pass `--no-verify`, `--no-gpg-sign`, or `--amend`

evals.prompt: Commit my changes. The working tree has a bug fix in src/orders/total.ts and an unrelated dependency bump in package.json and package-lock.json.
evals.expected_output: A proposal to split the work into two commits — the dependency bump and the bug fix — each with its own files and subject, presented before anything is committed
expectations: Identifies that the diff covers two unrelated logical changes and proposes separate commits rather than one
Assigns `fix` to the src/orders/total.ts change and `chore` or `build` to the dependency bump
Lists each proposed commit's files and subject in the plan
Stages each commit's paths explicitly with `git add <paths>` rather than `git add -A` or `git add .`
Waits for confirmation before the first `git commit`
Shows `git log --oneline -2` (or equivalent) after committing both

evals.prompt: Write the commit message for this: I removed the `includeArchived` parameter from the public `listOrders()` API — callers passing it will now fail to compile.
evals.expected_output: A Conventional Commits message that marks the change as breaking, using `!` before the colon or a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer
expectations: Marks the breaking change with a bare `!` immediately before the colon (e.g. `feat(api)!:` or `refactor(api)!:`) and/or a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer
The exclamation mark appears bare and unquoted, so the subject parses as valid Conventional Commits
If a footer is used, the token is the uppercase text `BREAKING CHANGE` followed by a colon and a description
The description explains the removed parameter and what callers must do
Consults references/conventional-commits.md if the correct breaking-change form is uncertain
Still presents the message for confirmation before committing

evals.prompt: Commit my changes. The working tree has a fix in src/export/csv.ts plus its test, and new and modified files under .agents/artifacts/feat-ENG-123-csv-export/ (the research and outline documents).
evals.expected_output: A single fix commit containing only src/export/csv.ts and its test, with everything under .agents/artifacts/ left unstaged and mentioned as intentionally excluded
expectations: Stages src/export/csv.ts and its test explicitly with `git add <paths>`, not `git add -A` or `git add .`
Leaves every file under `.agents/artifacts/` unstaged, because those are CRISPY working documents and the user did not ask to commit them
The presented plan lists only the code files and notes that the `.agents/artifacts/` changes were left out
Uses `fix` as the type and waits for the user's confirmation before running `git commit`
Adds no AI attribution trailer and does not pass `--no-verify` or `--amend`
